notes: IMPORTANT: none of the eight web searches ran; the shared web search budget was already used up, so all eight required searches (superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, pause or moratorium, China agreement, 'AI safety', official-site search, Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, 23 September 2026 letter) were refused. What was checked directly: (1) titles of all press releases on barr.house.gov from 3 January 2025 to 10 November 2026 (pages 1 to 15 of the press release list): no title concerns AI. Only titles were read, not the body of each release, so a passing AI remark inside a release would have been missed. (2) The campaign site barrforsenate.com home and issues pages: no mention of AI. (3) Congress.gov data for bills he sponsored and co-sponsored, scanned by title only: no bill with 'superintelligence' in the title, and no Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, appeared among the first 250 co-sponsored bills (which covered the 119th Congress portion seen) or the first 100 sponsored bills; the sponsored list has 223 items and the co-sponsored list 1,752, so the scan was not complete for older items, and the reading tool truncated long pages. (4) The two events: Barr is a House member until January 2027, so he was not eligible to sign a senators' letter or co-sponsor a Senate bill; no source seen shows him signing or co-sponsoring either, and I could not open the letter or the bill's co-sponsor list to confirm. Not checked at all: hearing remarks (he chairs a House Financial Services subcommittee and may have spoken about AI in banking there; the committee site refused access), floor speeches, interviews, op-eds and news coverage (Kentucky Lantern, Lexington Herald-Leader and Courier Journal searches were blocked or not reachable; LEX18 and WUKY searches showed nothing linking Barr to AI in the first page of results). No press release for H.R. 5927 was found in the press release titles. The record links to congress.gov for H.R. 3447 and H.R. 1121 were not opened (congress.gov returned 403); the facts came from the official api.congress.gov data.
